q: Who is God? — Nehemiah asked only to be “remembered” by God. What does this show you about how God cares for the faithful?
Who am I? — In your role, is there a “governor’s allowance” you have grown used to taking but shouldn’t?
How shall I respond? — If you were Liheng, how would you answer the admin manager?
lessons.jesus: Jesus had authority to command the wind and waves, yet he refused to turn stones into bread for himself (Matthew 4:3–4). He said, “the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many” (Mark 10:45). The King of kings did not exploit his privilege, but gave up everything for us.
lessons.pray: Lord, my position and resources are entrusted to me by you. Search my expense claims, my company card, and my dealings with suppliers. If there is anything I should not take, give me courage to let it go. When people say “everyone does it”, let me, because I fear you, not do so. I don’t seek to be remembered by people; I ask only that you remember me and show me your favour. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Check a recent expense claim: is every item clean?
Politely decline an inappropriate gift or personal perk
Do something for a colleague affected by cost-cutting
lessons.noon: “Remember me, my God, for all the good that I have done for this people” — Lord, right now I seek only your remembrance.

lessons.title: Drawing My 920 Relationship Map
lessons.theme: Review and correct this relationship stage, and see God’s work in my workplace relationships

v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

lessons.still: Take a sheet of paper, write your name in the middle, and draw a “0” around it. Say to the Lord: “Lord, in these months you have been at work in my relationships at work. Shine your light on me, so I can see clearly and be willing to change.”
teach: Paul writes, “doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself; each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.” This is our memory verse this week and a summary of the whole relationships stage. From managers and colleagues to team members and clients, God has been teaching us one thing: stop putting ourselves at the centre, and learn to count others better than ourselves. What fruit does such a life bear? “love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control.”

Company organisation charts are drawn from the top down, but a 920 relationship map is drawn outwards from the “0” at the centre: managers, colleagues, team members, clients, each one my “2”. Beside each line, write the fruit of the Spirit that relationship most needs. Then use the eight steps’ “review and correction” to ask five questions. Thinking: have I shifted from seeing them as tools or obstacles to seeing them as people God has given me? Life: in which relationship is my self-centredness most obvious? Daily living, relationships and ministry: which line needs repairing, and who is the one I am investing in?

When Nehemiah rebuilt the wall, each family repaired the section opposite its own house (Nehemiah 3:28), and in fifty-two days the wall was finished (Nehemiah 6:15). Repairing relationships works the same way. You don’t have to fix everything at once; begin with the section in front of you. Now open the “Workplace Health Self-Check” in the app and honestly rate yourself for this stage. Remember: review is not condemnation, and correction does not depend on your own strength. Success is not proof, failure is not condemnation, and the focus is on Jesus.
lessons.light: 321 Light: 920 — everyone connected to me is my “2”; I practise the self-emptied “0” and bear the “9” fruits of the Spirit. “Review and correction” in the eight steps means, under the Spirit’s light, taking one more step forward in thinking, life, daily living, relationships and ministry.
lessons.scene: Hemi is a foreman on a building site in Christchurch. After knocking off on Friday he sits in the site container office, following the course on his phone to draw his 920 relationship map: above him a difficult project manager, beside him two experienced carpenters, below him seven new labourers, and on the outer ring a client who complains constantly. When he reaches the line to the project manager, his pen stops for a long time.
q: Who is God? — Looking back over these months, in which workplace relationship have you seen God’s work most clearly?
Who am I? — On your 920 map, which line most needs “correction”? How does your self-centredness show itself there?
How shall I respond? — Like Hemi, draw your relationship map, complete the “Workplace Health Self-Check”, and choose one line to repair this week.
lessons.jesus: Jesus is the ultimate example of counting others better than himself: “who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant” (Philippians 2:6–7). He is the perfect “0”, and he gave his life for every “2”. The failures we see as we look back, he has already carried; the progress we see is all his grace.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for walking with me these months as I learned to relate to managers, colleagues, team members and clients. You see where I was proud, where I held back, and where I hurt people. Shine your light on my 920 map, and give me courage to repair the hardest line. Help me, in humility, to count others better than myself and bear the fruit of the Spirit in every relationship. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
